reading.body:
Six interactive estimators cover the questions that decide whether an AI project is viable: token cost, GPU memory, context window fit, training cost, energy and carbon, and return on investment.

The set is a decision layer, not a measurement layer. Each estimator shows its own arithmetic and states what it excludes, which means the value is in the assumptions being visible rather than in any single output. A cost or memory figure is only as good as the inputs a reader supplies.

For AI specifically, four of the six sit on the compute side: tokens, VRAM, context window, and training cost. Energy and carbon extend that chain to power, and return on investment closes it against revenue. That ordering matches how a project actually fails, first on memory or context limits, then on training and serving cost, then on the power behind them.

The data does not say how accurate any estimator is, what inputs they require, or whether they agree with each other. It records that six exist and that each discloses its exclusions. No worked examples, no benchmarks, and no results are given here, so nothing on this page supports a claim about what any specific model or workload would cost.
